title: Mastering Bull's-Eye Maculopathy: Pathophysiology & Clinical Management
summary: Bull's-eye maculopathy is a distinct phenotypic presentation characterized by a central area of RPE preservation surrounded by a ring of RPE atrophy. This pattern is pathognomonic for several hereditary and toxic retinal dystrophies requiring precise multimodal diagnostic differentiation.

sections.title: Definition & Etiology
sections.content: Bull's-eye maculopathy describes a specific fundus appearance: a central island of preserved RPE/foveal tissue, a ring of depigmentation/atrophy, and an outer ring of hyperpigmentation. Etiologically, it stems from metabolic disruption of the RPE/photoreceptor complex, often secondary to drug toxicity or genetic mutations (e.g., ABCA4, PROM1).

rows: ABCA4 mutation; early onset; dark choroid

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol
content: Step 1: Baseline Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) for baseline mapping.
Step 2: SD-OCT (horizontal/vertical macular scans) to check for EZ/OS layer attenuation.
Step 3: 10-2 Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) for pericentral scotomas.
Step 4: mfERG for functional assessment of central retinal health.
Step 5: Fundus photography (Color) to document the classic ring appearance.

sections.title: Recent Advances: The AAO 2016 Recommendations
content: Shifted screening paradigm from 'dosage' to 'functional imaging' (OCT/FAF/mfERG).
Maximal daily dose capped at 5.0 mg/kg of real weight.
Emphasis on early detection before the 'Bull's-eye' becomes visible on color fundus exam.
High-risk patients (Asian descent, kidney disease) require more frequent, rigorous screening.
